rashi: Leyashuv. hu yov haamur beyorede mitzrayim, ki chol hammishpachot nikreu al shem yorede mitzrayim, vehannoladin misham vahalea lo nikreu hammishpachot al shemam, chutz mimmishpechot efrayim umenashe shennoledu chullam bemitzrayim, veard venaaman bene vela ben binyamin; umatzati visodo shel rabbi moshe haddarshan, sheyyorda imman mimmitzrayim keshehayeta meubberet mehem, lechach nechleku lemishpachot kechetzron vechamul shehayu vene vanim lihuda, vechever umalkiel shehayu vene vanim shel asher; veim aggada hi hare tov, veim lav, omer ani shehayu levela bene vanim harbe, umishenayim hallalu, ard venaaman, yotza mikkol echad mishpacha rabba, venikreu toledot shear habbanim al shem bela, vetoledot hashenayim hallalu nikreu al shemam, vechen ani omer bivne machir shennechleku lishte mishpachot, achat nikret al shemo, veachat nikret al shem gilad beno; chamesh mishpachot chaseru mibbanav shel binyamin, kan nitkayyema miktzat nevuat immo shekkeraattu ven oni — ben aninuti, uvefilegesh begiva (Shoftim 20) nitkayyema kulla. zo matzati visodo shel ra' moshe haddarshan:

Veelle bene shutalach vegomer'. shear bene shutelach nikreu toledotehem al shem shutelach, umeeran yotza mishpacha rabba venikret al shemo, venechshevu vene shutelach lishte mishpachot, tze vachashov vetimtza befarasha zo chamishim vesheva mishpachot umibbene levi shemone hare shishim vechamesh, vezehu shenneemar "ki attem hamat" vego' — hei meat, chamesh attem chaserim mimmishpechot kol haammim, shehen shivim. af zo hevanti misodo shel rabbi moshe haddarshan, ach hutzrachti lifchot ulehosif bidvarav:
Laachiram. hu echi sheyyarad lemitzrayim, ulefi shennikra al shem yosef shehaya achiv veram mimmennu nikra achiram:
Lishfufam. hu muppim, al shem shehaya yosef shafuf ben haummot:
Leshucham. hu chushim:

Ki tzorarim hem lachem vegomer' al devar peor. shehifkiru benotehem liznut, kede lehatotechem achar peor. veet moav lo tzivva lehashmid, mippene rut shehayeta atida latzet mehem, kidamrinan bevava kamma (Lach 2):
Levet avotam. al shevet haav yityachasu velo achar haem (Bava Batra 109):
Kala sheeri. nitavva besari ulevavi lecha:
Kala sheeri. leshon taava, kemo "kolta litshuatecha nafshi" (Tehillim 119:81):
targum: Ishtetza gushemi velibbevi takifa devachen livevi vechulaki elaha lealma:

rashi: Zone mimmekka. nifrad mimmecha:
targum: Arum ha rashiaya di mitrachakin minach yovdun shetzeta kol detae min batar dechaltach:

rashi: Malachotecha. shelichutecha, ruach hakkodesh habba belibbi lemor:
targum: Vaana lemikrav baAdonai li tav shavyet baAdonai elohim ruchetzani leishtaaya letzadikaya kulehon pikude shelichutach:

rashi: Vayyihyu lenes. leot ulezikkaron, "lemaan asher lo yikrav ish zar" (Bamidbar 17) lachalok od al hakkehunna:

targum: Metul di vememeri itrei vaashezevineh asagvineh metul deyada shemi:
Yetzele kodamay vaana ane yateh imeh ana veakta eftzineh vaayakrineh:
Orichut yomin asbeineh veachmineh befurekani:

rashi: Veshem bat asher sarach. lefi shehayeta kayyemet bechayyeha menaah kan (seder olam):
Elle mishpechot levi. chaser kan mishpechot hashimi vehaazzieli uketzat min hayyitzhari:

Asher yolda otah lelevi bemitzrayim. ledatah bemitzrayim veen horatah bemitzrayim, keshennichnesu letoch hachoma yeladatta, vehi hishlima minyan shivim, shehare vifratan e atta motze ella shishim vatesha:

Ki lo hotpakedu betoch bene yisrael. lihyot nimnin bene esrim shana, ma taam? ki lo natan laham nachalah, vehannimnin mibben esrim shana hayu vene nachala, shenneemar "ish lefi fekudav yuttan nachalato":

Uveelle lo haya ish vegomer'. aval al hannashim lo nigzera gezerat hamraggelim, lefi shehen hayu mechabbevot et haaretz, haanashim omerim nittena rosh venashuva mitzrayma, vehannashim omerot "tena lanu achuzza", lechach nismecha farashat benot tzelofchad lechan (tanchuma):
Lishero hakkarov elav mimmishpachto. veen mishpacha keruya ella mitztzad haav (Sham 109):

Ale el har haavarim. lamma nismecha lechan? kevan sheamar hakkabbah naton titten lahem, amar oti tzivva hammakom lehanchil, shemma huttera haggezera veekkanes laaretz? amar lo hakkabbah gezerati bimkomah omedet. daa — kevan shennichnas moshe lenachalat bene gad uvene reuven samach veamar, kimdumme shehuttar li nidri; mashal lemelech sheggazar al beno shello yikkanes lefetach palatin shello, nichnas lashaar vehu acharav, lechatzer vehu acharav, latteraklin vehu acharav, kevan shebba likkanes lakkiton, amar lo beni mikkan vaelach atta asur likkanes (sifre):
Hem me merivat kadesh. hem levaddam — en bahem avon acher; daa — hem shehimru vemara, hem hayu shehimru veyam suf, hem atzmam shehimru vemidbar tzin:

Asher yetze lifnehem. lo chederech malche haummot sheyyoshevim bevattehem umeshallechin et chayyalotehem lammilchama, ella kemo sheasiti ani, shennilchamti vesichon uveog, shenneemar (Bamidbar 21) "al tira oto", uchederech sheasa yehoshua, shenneemar "vayyelech yehoshua elav vayyomer lo halanu atta" vego' (Yehoshua 5), vechen bedavid hu omer (Shmuel 1 18) "ki hu yotze vava lifnehem" — yotze barosh venichnas barosh (sifre):
Vaasher yotziem. bizchuyyotav:
Vaasher yeviem. bizchuyyotav. daa — vashar yabiam, shello taase lo kederech sheatta ose li, sheeni machnisan laaretz (yalkut shemauni):
Vetzivvita oto. al yisrael, da shettarchanin hem, sarvanim hem, al menat shettekabbel alecha (Sifre Bamidbar 11):
Venatatta mehodecha alav. ze kerun or panim:
Mehodecha. velo kol hodecha, umatzinu lemedin pene moshe kachamma pene yehoshua kallevana (Sifre; Bava Batra 75):
Lemaan yishmeu kol adat bene yisrael. sheyyihyu nohagin bo kavod veyira, kederech shennohagin becha:
Et hakkeves echad. aapi shekkevar neemar befarashat veatta tetzavve "veze asher taase" vego' (Shemot 29 Lach), hi hayeta azhara lime hammilluim vechan tzivva laddorot:
Solet lemincha. minchat nesachim:

Haasuya behar sinay. keotan shennaasu bime hammilluim; daa — hashih bahar siny, hikkish olat tamid leolat har sinay — otah shennitkorva lifne mattan tora — shekkatuv bah (Sham 24) "vayyashom baaganot", melammed shetteuna keli (sifre):
Venisko. yayin:
Bakkodesh hassech. al hammizbeach yitnassechu:
Nesech shechar. yayin hamshakker, perat leyayin miggitto (Bava Batra 97):
Reach nichoach. nachat ruach lefanay sheamarti venaasa retzoni (sifre):

Olat shabbat beshabbatto. velo olat shabbat zo beshabbat acheret, hare shello hikriv beshabbat zo shomea ani yakriv shettayim lashabbat habbaa, tal "beshabbatto", maggid sheim avar yomo batel korbano (sifre):
Al olat hattamid. ellu musafin, levad otan shene chevasim shel olat hattamid, umaggid sheen kerevin ella ben shene hattemidin, vechen bechol hammusafin neemar al olat hattamid letalmud ze:
Ushelosha esronim. kemishpat niske far, shekken hen ketzuvin befarashat nesachim:
Zot olat chodesh bechodsho. sheim avar yomo batel korbano veshuv en lo tashlumin:

Useir izzim vegomer'. kol seire hammusafin bain lechapper al tumat mikdash vekadashav, hakkol kemo shemmeforash bemassechet shevuot (Daf 9), venishtanna seir rosh chodesh shenneemar bo "laAdonai"; lelammedcha shemmechapper al sheen bo yedia lo vattechilla velo vassof — sheen makkir bachete ella hakkabbah vilvad, ushear hasseirim lemedin mimmenu; umidrasho baaggada, amar hakkabbah haviu chappara alay al shemmiatti et hayyareach (Chullin 60):
Al olat hattamid yease. kol hakkorban hazze:
Venisko. en "venisko" musav al hassair, sheen nesachim lechattat:
Kol melechet avoda. afillu melacha hatztzericha lachem, kegon davar haaved, hammuttar bechullo shel moed, asura beyt:
Parim. keneged avraham shenneemar "veel habbakar ratz avraham" (Bereshit 18):
Ailim. keneged elo shel yitzchak:
Chevasim. keneged yaakov shenneemar "vehakkesavim hifrid yaakov" (Sham 30); bisodo shel ra' moshe haddarshan raiti zot:
Kaelle taasu layyom. shello yihyu fochatin veholechin kefare hechag (sifre):
Temimim yihyu lachem veniskehem. af hannesachim yihyu temimim, lamedu rabbotenu mikkan shehayyayin sheheela kemachin pasul linsachim (Sham 87):
Millevad olat hachodesh. musefe rosh chodesh shehu veyom rosh hashana:
Millevad chattat hakkippurim. sair hannaase bifnim haamur beachare mot, sheggam hu chattat:
Veolat hattamid. umillevad olat hattamid taasu olot hallalu:

Veniskehem. musav al hammusafin hakketuvim veal taasu, vehu leshon tzivvuy — millevad olat hattamid uminchatah taasu et elle veniskehem, vechen kol niskehem haamurim bechol hammoadot chutz mishel korbenot hechag, shekkol veniskah, veniskehem, unesacheha shebbahem musabbim al hattamid, veenan leshon tzivvuy, shehare niskehem shel musafin ketuvin leatzman bechol yom vayom:
Uminchatam veniskehem lapparim. pare hechag shivim hem keneged shivim ummot, umitmaatim veholechim, siman kelaya hi lahem, uvime hammikdash hayu meginnim alehem min hayyissurin (Socha 55):

Velakkevasim. keneged yisrael shennikreu "se fezura" (Yirmeyahu 50), vehem kevuim, uminyanam tishim ushemona, lechallot mehem tishim ushemone kelalot shebbemishne tora; basheni neemar veniskehem al shene temide hayyom, velo shinna hallashon ella lidrosh, kemo sheameru rabbotenu zili (sifre; shabbat kn) basheni veniskehem, bashishi unesacheha, bashevii kemishpatam, mem yod mem hare chan mayim, remez lenissuch hammayim min hattora bechag:

Atzeret tihye lachem. atzurim baasiyyat melacha; daa, atzarat — itzru millatzet, melammed shettaun lina; umidrasho vaaggada lefi shekkol yemot haregel hikrivu cheneged shivim ummot, uvain lalechet, amar lahem hammakom bevakkasha mikkem asu li seuda ketanna kede sheehane mikkem (Socha 55):

Par echad ayil echad. ellu cheneged yisrael, hitakkevu li meat od, uleshon chibba hu ze, kevanim hanniftarim meavihem vehu omer lahem kasha alay peredatchem, akkevu od yom echad, mashal lemelech sheasa seuda chu', kidita vemassechet sukka (sham); uvemidrash rabbi tanchuma: limmeda tora derech eretz shemmi sheyyesh lo achsenay yom rishon yaachilennu petumot, lemachar yaachilennu dagim, lemachar besar behema, lemachar maachilo kitnit, lemachar maachilo yarak, pochet veholech kefare hechag:
Elle taasu lh' bemoadechem. davar hakkatzuv lechova:

Levad minnidrechem. im batem liddor korbanot baregel, mitzva hi beyedchem, o nedarim o nedavot shennedartem kol hashana, hakrivum baregel, shemma yikshe lo lachazor velaalot lirushalayim ulehakriv nedarav venimtza over beval teacher:

Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 12:98-: The sage said, always set your mind that truth is before you - meaning, that he make a sign for himself, when coming to engage in business, that he remember and not speak falsehood, and write it down and bring it before him and look at it before his dealings - and likewise write it in his study hall and on his table, that he remember and not speak falsehood, so that he not forget and fail to know a true matter. And so a certain sage did - he wrote on the walls above, "remember the day of your death and do not sin."

And whoever speaks only truth shall live and prolong his days and be saved from all evil - and proof from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, when he leaped, and so on, that the Angel of Death had no power over him in his lifetime, for he never in all his days spoke any falsehood or lie, and he is still in the Garden of Eden in his lifetime (Ketubot 77b) - based on the verse (Jeremiah 10:10), "but the LORD God is truth, He is the living God and the everlasting King." And if he speaks only truth he shall be saved all his days from all evil, as it is written (Malachi 2:6), "the Torah of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips; he walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and turned many away from iniquity. For the priest's lips should guard knowledge... for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" - for the supernal angels have the form of truth and are not in bodies, and souls are hewn from them like light, while souls are like bodies - therefore they know hidden things only a little, and only in a nighttime vision when the soul is not occupied with the needs of the body. And whoever knows the secret of the soul shall testify to the matter, that dreams are from the aspect of thoughts - "your thoughts upon your bed arose" (Daniel 2:29) - and dreams come through the angel who accompanies people, and since not all thoughts are true, not all dreams are true. And whoever accustoms himself to having all his thoughts be true shall also see, at night, visions of truth and know future things, like the angels.

For one who speaks truth there is no greater virtue - therefore, "the sum of Your word is truth" (Psalms 119:160), and he warned, "keep far from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7). Also, a person's hints [and gestures] should be true, for the reward of truth is very great. Therefore a person should accustom himself to walk in truth, and to study Torah in order to know the truth, and in order to be able to perform the commandments truly and according to their halachah - and he should always acknowledge the truth, and even learn matters of aggadah that involve no fulfillment of a commandment, in order that his heart believe the true matter. Do not be ashamed to accept the truth from wherever it comes, even from the smallest of the small and the most despised of the despised - accept the truth from him, for a good pearl in the hand of a small and despised person is always as valuable as a pearl.

Now, because of our sins, since the exile has lasted overly long, Israel must separate from the vanities of the world and hold fast to the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is truth, and sanctify themselves even in what is permitted to them, and not lie either to a Jew or to a gentile, and not deceive him in any matter, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:13), "the remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth," and it is written (Hosea 2:25), "and I will sow her for Myself in the land" - does not a person who sows one measure find several measures? So the Holy One, blessed be He, sows Israel in the lands so that converts be added to them (Pesachim 87b) - and as long as they conduct themselves with deceit, who would cleave to them? Now, the Holy One, blessed be He, was strict about the theft of the wicked, as it is said (Genesis 6:11), "and the earth was filled with violence."

And there was a story of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach, who bought a donkey from a certain Ishmaelite. His students went and found a precious stone hanging from its neck, and brought the stone to Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach and said to him, "the blessing of the LORD makes rich" (Proverbs 10:22). He said to them, I bought a donkey, I did not buy a precious stone - and he returned it to that Ishmaelite, and that Ishmaelite exclaimed, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of Rabbi Shimon ben Shetach" (Devarim Rabbah 3:3). And so it is found in the Jerusalem Talmud (Bava Metzia, chapter 2, halachah 5), that the early sages bought wheat from gentiles and found in it a bundle of coins, and returned it to them, and the gentiles opened it and said, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of the Jews." And there are many such stories that warn concerning the sanctification of the blessed Name.

And when there is truth below, then the Name shall look with righteousness upon the earth, as it is said (Psalms 85:12), "truth shall spring up from the earth, and righteousness shall look down from heaven" - therefore hold fast to truth, and whether the matter be bad or good, do not abandon truth, and rely on the Faithful One, as it is written (Deuteronomy 7:9), "and you shall know that the LORD your God," and so on, "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and mercy," and so on - and what is His faithfulness, that He keeps the covenant? If there is a righteous person who sinned, He exacts his recompense in this world. And this is a clear matter, that it is better for the righteous to be judged even with the sufferings of Job in his body all his days - which is something despicable and in the short time he is in this world - and to give him his good reward in the honored thing, in the supernal world, to reach supernal levels, in the good time that is entirely long and never ceases - this is better for the righteous than to have been complete in this world and not have his sins repaid in this world, and be judged in the World to Come with the sufferings of Gehinnom, or, because of his sin, have his soul diminished from its level in the world of souls, and cleave to the splendor of the supernal levels, for which pleasure there is no comparison or likeness. And to the wicked, they give their recompense in a small, ceasing pleasure, in the short world, which is this world, while the sin is reserved for the long world, and with great suffering, which is Gehinnom, for which suffering there is no comparison - and Scripture is explicit (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them" - the explanation is that the Holy One, blessed be He, repays the wicked their merits in this world, in order to destroy them for the World to Come. And it further says, "He will not delay [repaying] one who hates Him; He will repay him to his face" - this is said of the righteous, that He repays his sins in this world so that he have the World to Come. May the Merciful One guide us in His truth, and bring us into His chambers, to reach the light where the hiding place of His strength and the beauty of His splendor are - to this point.
And with this the chapter is concluded:

Concerning the punishment of the group of slanderers, and its parts - and because the discourse is longer in this matter, we saw fit to devote a chapter of its own to it. And it is said in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Metzora 1): three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come - the four commoners are Balaam, Doeg, Achitophel, and Gehazi - you find that these were all pushed into Gehinnom because of the speech of their mouths - and it brings proof for each and every one, and in order not to be lengthy we shall not copy their wording.

Further there, Rabbi Pedat said, a covenant is made with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the world, that whoever speaks slander shall be struck with leprosy - from where? From that which calls this matter "this shall be the law of the leper [metzora]" [interpreted as] "the law of one who brings forth an evil name [motzi shem ra]." Our Rabbis said, plagues come upon a person only because of the slander that he utters from his mouth - and the holy spirit cries out and says (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin" - to strike your body - "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - do not say before the one appointed over you, "the speech was an error," because every single word that emerges from your mouth is written in a book, whether good or evil, whether unwitting or deliberate - and from where do we know this is so? As it is said (Malachi 3:16), "then those who feared the LORD spoke, each to his neighbor, and the LORD listened and heard, and it was written in a book of remembrance before Him, for those who feared the LORD and thought upon His Name." And likewise concerning the measure of retribution, David said (Psalms 139:2), "You know my sitting down and my rising up; You understand my thought from afar," and Job likewise said (Job 14:16), "for now You count my steps," and (13:27), "and You engrave marks on the soles of my feet" - "why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands" - these are the hands and the body that are struck with leprosy.

And in Devarim Rabbah (Parashat Ki Teitzei), in explaining this verse, "do not let your mouth cause [your flesh] to sin," as expounded - however, at the end of the verse, "and do not say before the angel that it was an error," they said, of blessed memory, that you should not say, I shall go and speak slander and no creature will know - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, know that I send an angel who stands beside you and writes down everything you speak about your fellow - from where? As it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:20), "even in your knowledge, do not curse the king" - why? "For a bird of the heavens shall carry the voice" - and what is "a possessor of wings shall tell the matter"? These are the angels of whom it is written, "six wings for each one" (Isaiah 6:2) - to this point.

And the pious master Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz, peace be upon him, wrote, in the Mishnah "whoever profanes the Name of Heaven in secret" (Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 4), a fitting matter concerning slander, alongside this teaching that explains the verse "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - that every single word is written down - and I saw fit to copy it here, in these words: and it appears to me that included in "profaning the Name of Heaven in secret" is the slanderer, because there are found in his wings the dust of three severe transgressions, whose root, in each of them, one must be killed rather than transgress - as they said, of blessed memory (Arachin 15b): concerning idolatry it is written (Exodus 32:31), "please, this people has sinned a great sin"; concerning forbidden relations (Genesis 39:9), "how then could I do this great evil"; concerning bloodshed it is written (ibid. 4:13), "my iniquity is greater than can be borne"; and concerning slander it is written (Psalms 12:4), "a tongue that speaks great things."

And do not think that he said this by way of exaggeration, but by way of true precision. This is because the idol worshippers would say, the LORD does not see us, and therefore they were drawn after those services, to find favor in the eyes of the male and female deities, according to their corrupted view. Now, the slanderer of his fellow - when he hears the sound of his footsteps, he falls silent in his words and changes his speech, and once he has passed from before him, he returns to his corruption, not thinking of the One whose glory fills the whole earth, whose eyes everywhere watch the evil and the good (Proverbs 15:3). And the adulterous woman "eats, and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no wrong" (Proverbs 30:20) - and the slanderer shows a pleasant countenance to his fellow to his face, while within him he sets his ambush, and as soon as he passes, mocks him and makes him a trampling ground for the sword of his tongue. And bloodshed needs no explanation, for it is his foundation, all the more so if he whitens [shames] his face in public. And since this is so, there is no greater desecration of the Name than this, and therefore they are punished openly, as it is said (Numbers 12:15), "and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in" - for they all knew the greatness of slander, even though it was in secret and unwitting - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:19-: And in the Yalkut (Parashat Devarim, siman 788), concerning "and Chatzerot" (Deuteronomy 1:1), this teaching concerning Miriam is explained further, in these words: "and Chatzerot" - He said to them, should you not have learned from what I did to Miriam in Chatzerot? If I did not show favor to Miriam the righteous, an a fortiori argument for the rest of the people - if Miriam, who spoke only of her brother, who was younger than her, was punished so, one who speaks of one greater than himself, all the more so. Another interpretation: if Miriam, when she spoke, was heard by no creature but the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, as it is said, "and the LORD heard," and was punished so, one who speaks disparagingly of his fellow in public, all the more so - to this point. And he says "another interpretation," and did not combine them into one, as in the previous Sifrei teaching, to teach us that whichever of these aspects occurs in reality - such as a wise, righteous person who wishes to speak slander of one lesser than himself, or who speaks between himself and his fellow where no creature heard - each and every aspect carries a punishment for slander.

And in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 17:3) it further says, plagues come because of ten things: idolatry, forbidden relations, bloodshed, desecration of the Name, cursing the Name, robbing the public, robbing what is not one's own, arrogance, slanderers, and the evil eye - and it proves all these from verses. And in Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 4) they are brought, except with some variation between them, and it is not relevant to our matter, so we have not copied its wording.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, page 206a) it says that plagues come because of eleven things, in these words: idolatry, cursing the Name, forbidden relations, theft, slander, false testimony, a judge who perverts judgment, a vain oath, one who enters his fellow's boundary, one who plans evil schemes, and one who sows discord among brothers - and some say, also the evil eye - to this point, and it proves all these with proofs - see there.

And in Pesachim (118a) they said, of blessed memory: Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, whoever speaks slander, whoever accepts slander, and whoever testifies falsely against his fellow, deserves to be cast to the dogs, as it is said (Exodus 22:30), "you shall cast it to the dogs," and it is written right after (ibid. 23:1), "you shall not accept a false report" - and it reads it as "you shall not cause [others] to accept" - to this point. And in Tractate Arachin (16a) they count only seven [things for which plagues come] - and this requires examination.

Further, there in that same tractate and chapter (15b), concerning the punishment of slander, Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva, whoever speaks slander deserves to be stoned with stones - it is written here (Psalms 101:5), "him I will destroy [atzmit]" - and it is written there (Lamentations 3:53), "they have cut off [tzamtu] my life in the pit, and cast a stone at me." And when you recall what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 59b, Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 110a) and the Ra'aya Meheimna concerning stoning, you shall know to what extent the blemish and power of slander reaches.

Further there, Reish Lakish said, whoever speaks slander magnifies sins reaching to the heavens, as it is said (Psalms 73:9), "they have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth" - and his intent is concerning the attribute called "Shamayim" [Heaven], as they said in the Bahir (letter 100), "and You shall hear in heaven" (1 Kings 8:32) - for it is known that he blemishes "the earth" of life, as explained above, and it teaches us that the blemish also ascends to "the heavens."

Further there, Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, what is the remedy for slanderers? If he is a Torah scholar, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life" - and "tongue" [here in the preceding half of the verse] refers only to slander, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" - and "tree of life" refers only to Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it." And if he is an ignorant person, let him humble his mind, as it is said (ibid. 15:4), "but perversity in it is a break in the spirit." Rabbi Abba bar Chanina said, one who has already spoken it has no remedy, for David has already cut him off by the holy spirit, as it is said (Psalms 12:4), "may the LORD cut off all flattering lips."

And the teaching of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina, who gave a remedy for slander through Torah and through humility of spirit, certainly has reasoning, and it is a plausible reason - for Torah is more significant than all offerings. Indeed, even the sin of desecration of the Name, in the teaching concerning the house of Eli (1 Samuel 3:14), "if the iniquity of the house of Eli shall be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever" - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Rosh Hashanah 18a), that it shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it is atoned for through words of Torah, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 80b). And likewise humility is equal to all the offerings, as it is said (Psalms 51:19), "the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit," as they explained, of blessed memory (Sotah 5b), concerning humility, that it is accounted to him as though he offered all the offerings. If so, since this one humbles his spirit and his pride, he shall be atoned for - for the sin of slander comes from pride and willfulness, and therefore he does not regard people as anything, and speaks whatever comes to his mouth - and therefore his remedy is in humbling himself, measure for measure.

And even according to the words of Rabbi Abba bar Chanina, who said there is no remedy for it, it is possible that his sin was great, along the lines of Doeg the Edomite, who, although great in Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, nevertheless called him wicked - "and to the wicked, God said, what have you to do with declaring My statutes" (Psalms 50:16) - and they said in the chapter "Chelek" (Sanhedrin 106b) that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Doeg, when you reach the passage of murderers and the passage of slanderers, what do you expound in them? "And you take My covenant in your mouth" - Rabbi Ami said, Doeg's Torah was only from the lips outward.

Also, it is possible to resolve this, as Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, author of Menorat HaMaor, resolved it (letter 50): what it says, that there is a remedy for it, refers to one not habituated, who has a remedy so as not to continue - but one constant in the matter, "his hand still stretched out," is cut off in his sin. And it is possible to broaden his words with what Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, explained in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 3, letter 202), giving the reason that the slanderer's sin is greater than idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed (Arachin 15b) - he gives five reasons for the matter, one of them being that the master of the tongue's repentance is difficult, for it is possible he spoke slander about many and does not know who they are in order to appease them. Further, that from the abundance of his habit it is impossible for him to repent properly, for speaking slander has become second nature to him. For this reason we can say there is no remedy for it. And concerning something similar to this, it also says in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 53a) that he has no repentance - and this is difficult, for it is written (Leviticus 14:2), "on the day of his cleansing, he shall be brought to the priest" - rather, certainly it speaks of one for whom speaking slander has become second nature, and it is impossible for him to be purified from it - and the intent of saying "he has no repentance" is that his repentance is difficult, until he repents properly.

And in Devarim Rabbah (Parashat Shoftim, 9) it says that in the days of Saul they did not merit the building of the Temple because there were slanderers among them, Doeg and the Ziphites. And in the days of Ahab, although they were idol-worshippers, because there was no slander among them, they were victorious in war. Further there, another interpretation: Rabbi Muna said, whoever speaks slander removes the Shechinah from below to above. Know that this is so from what David says (Psalms 57:5), "my soul is among lions, I lie among those who blaze - the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword" - what is written after it? (57:6) "be exalted above the heavens, O God," and so on. David said, Master of the universe, what is the Shechinah doing below? Remove the Shechinah to the firmament - to this point.

See how severe slander is, more severe than bloodshed, forbidden relations, and idolatry - than bloodshed, as it is written (Genesis 4:13), "my iniquity is greater than can be borne"; than forbidden relations, as it is written (ibid. 39:9), "how then could I do this great evil"; than idolatry, as it is written (Exodus 32:31), "please, this people has sinned a great sin." But concerning slanderers, neither "great" [masculine] nor "greata" [feminine misuse] is written, but "great things" [plural], as it is said (Psalms 12:4), "may the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things" - therefore it is said (Proverbs 18:21), "death and life are in the hand of the tongue."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:31-: Another interpretation: "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" - do not say, since permission has been given to me to speak, I shall say whatever I wish - the Torah has already warned you, as it is said (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil" - and lest you say, you are causing yourself loss - no, rather you gain - and the holy spirit cries out (Proverbs 21:23), "he who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul [nafsho] from troubles [mitzarot]" - do not read "mitzarot" but "mi-tzara'at nafsho" [from the leprosy of his soul] - to this point.

Now, in what this teaching says at its end, "from the leprosy of his soul," we find a fine resolution - for we see that many people speak slander and have no plagues or leprosy - rather, certainly the leprosy and the plague are fixed in the soul: when the soul ascends every night, all the holy ones keep away from it and proclaim concerning it that it is impure, as it says (Leviticus 13:45), "and he shall cry, unclean, unclean" - or after its departure from this world, if it did not do proper repentance.

And somewhat inclining toward this explanation are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Parashat Ki Tazria, page 46b) - although he does not change the word "mitzarot" from its plain meaning, nevertheless from the general matter something is heard along the lines of what is being expounded, in these words, on the verse (Genesis 2:7), "and man became a living soul" - he explains there that "a living soul" is the neshamah, which is the highest level among the levels of holiness in man. And he says afterward: come and see, at every time this holy soul cleaves to a person, he is beloved of his Master, how many guards guard him from every side, he is marked for good above and below, and the holy Shechinah rests upon him - but at the time he strays from his ways, the Shechinah withdraws from him, and the holy soul does not cleave to him, and from the side of the strong evil serpent this spirit is aroused, which roams and goes through the world, for it rests only in a place from which supernal holiness has withdrawn - and then the person is defiled and blemished in his flesh, in the appearance of his face, in everything.

And come and see, because this living soul is holy, supernal - when the holy land [i.e., Malchut] draws it within itself and it is included, then we call it neshamah, and this is what ascends above and speaks before the holy King, and enters all gates, and none can stop its hand - and therefore it is called "the speaking spirit," for all other souls have no permission to speak before the King except this one. And therefore the Torah proclaimed and said, "guard your tongue from evil," and so on, and it is written, "he who guards his mouth and his tongue" - because if his lips and his tongue speak evil words, those words ascend above, and at the time they ascend, all proclaim and say, clear away from around the evil word of so-and-so, make room for the path of the strong serpent - then the holy soul is removed from him and withdraws and cannot speak, as it is said (Psalms 39:3), "I was mute with silence, I held my peace" - and that soul ascends in shame, in the distress of everything, and they do not give it a place as before - and therefore it is written, "he who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from troubles" - "his soul" certainly, that which used to speak became silent because of the evil speech, and then the serpent is summoned, for everything returns to its place. And when that evil word ascends by known paths and stands before the strong serpent, how many spirits are aroused in the world, and a spirit descends from that side and finds that this person has been aroused with an evil word, and behold, the holy speaking spirit has departed from him, and then it rests upon him and defiles him, and then he becomes "closed up" [i.e., leprous].

Just as this person's punishment is because of the evil word, so his punishment is for a good word that comes to his hand and he could speak it, because he blemishes that speaking spirit - for it was prepared to speak above and to speak below, and all in holiness - all the more so if a nation walks in a crooked path and he could speak to them and stays silent and does not speak, as I have said, "I was mute with silence, I held my peace, [even] from good, and my pain was stirred" (Psalms 39:3, adapted), with the plagues of impurity - and this is what King David said concerning this, "I was struck and turned away from Him," as it is written (Psalms 86:16), "turn to me and be gracious to me," as it is said (Numbers 12:10), "and Aaron turned" - to this point. And we have learned from this teaching how great is the punishment of slander.

In Parashat "this shall be the law of the leper," at its beginning, in these words: Rabbi Chiya said, whoever utters slander, all his limbs are defiled, and he shall appear to need to be shut in [as a leper], because that evil word ascends and arouses an impure spirit and it becomes defiled - it comes to be defiled, they defile him - through a word below, another word is aroused.

Further there, Rabbi Yehudah said, "this shall be the law of" - certainly, corresponding to this, to exact punishment from him, "the one who brings forth an evil name" - "on the day of his cleansing, he shall be brought to the priest" - what does this teach us? It implies that whoever has slander, his prayer does not enter before the Holy One, blessed be He, for an impure spirit has been aroused against him. Once he returns in repentance and accepts repentance upon himself, what is written? "On the day of his cleansing, he shall be brought to the priest" - to this point.

And it says, "once he returns in repentance" and "accepts repentance" - for two kinds of repentance are needed: the first, immediate repentance, which is submission, as they explained, of blessed memory (Proverbs 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it is a break in the spirit" - and therefore the Torah commanded hyssop, which indicates lowliness and submission. And further, "accepts repentance upon himself" - meaning, to accept upon himself not to return again to that sin, as it says (Psalms 85:9), "and let them not return to folly."

And included in the repentance needed for slander is that he make himself mute concerning worldly matters, as though he had no tongue - for concerning the master of the tongue it is said (Psalms 12:4), "may the LORD cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things" - and the intent of "cut off" is explained as meaning that his tongue is cut off in Gehinnom as many times as he spoke slander, along the lines of what is done for other transgressions, that the limb with which he sinned is judged until all that evil he did is digested - and therefore he must cut off his own tongue from speaking while still alive, and suffer in exchange for what he enjoyed.

And after we have spoken of the punishment of slander, let us speak of the parts of slander - and although we have not written everything found in the words of our Rabbis, so as not to be lengthy, this reminder is enough for the wise to arouse his heart to repent. And I saw fit to condense the words of Rabbeinu Yonah in the Gate of Repentance and the other authors who write on this matter.

The first part of slander, concerning which we were commanded in the Torah not to speak it and not to accept it, as it is said (Exodus 23:1), "you shall not accept a false report" - its essence is one who speaks disparagingly of his fellow, even if he speaks the truth - for if he speaks falsely, he is found to bring forth an evil name. And one who speaks disparagingly of his fellow intends to make his reputation stink and disgrace him, and therefore reveals the abominations of his ancestors, even if not in his presence - and this is the group of true slanderers. If he was a penitent and one speaks of his earlier sins, whether not in his presence or in his presence, his punishment is great, for one who repents has his sins made into merits, and this shames him, and it is not fitting. And further, others who hear this shame of a penitent will refrain and not repent - and it is found that he closes the door of repentance.

And Rabbeinu Yonah, of blessed memory, wrote that in one respect the sin of one who speaks slander about a true matter is greater than one who speaks a false matter - for people will believe what he says about his fellow to be honest words, and his stench will rise before them, and he will be despised in their eyes, even if he regretted his sin and repented - his blemish shall remain in people's mouths. And if a person sees his fellow transgress a matter of Torah in secret, he should not reveal his sin publicly, for perhaps he repented - especially if he is a single witness, for one who testifies alone against his fellow, they give him stripes for rebellion - and it is not fitting to reveal it except to a discreet sage who will not tell the rest of the masses - and if he knows they will believe him like the words of two witnesses, then he may tell it, so that that sage hate him - so they said in "Arvei Pesachim" (113b) - but it is permitted to distance oneself from his company and hate him until one knows that he has turned from his evil way.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:43-: And concerning matters between a person and his fellow, such as theft, oppression, and fraud, he may tell these matters to people, for they said, of blessed memory (Ketubot 87b), that one witness obligates him to an oath. And if the sinner is a Torah scholar and a God-fearing man, it is fitting to think of him that he truly repented, as they explained, of blessed memory (Berachot 19a), "if you saw a Torah scholar commit a transgression by day, do not think ill of him at night, for he certainly repented." And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tikkunei Zohar, page 141b), that concerning this it is said (Deuteronomy 21:23), "his corpse shall not remain overnight on the tree" - concerning the corpse of the sin he committed on the Tree of Life, for he certainly repented. And concerning this we find that Joseph the righteous was punished for bringing an evil report of his brothers to his father, and so they said in Bereshit Rabbah (84:7) on the verse (Genesis 37:2), "and Joseph brought," as Rashi explains, and for all three [reports] he was struck.

But a man whom we know to be completely wicked, with no fear of God before his eyes, it is permitted to publicize him and speak disparagingly of him, to make transgressors stink in people's eyes, so that the souls of the listeners be disgusted by evil deeds - as it is said (Proverbs 8:13), "the fear of the LORD is to hate evil" - and they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 52a), a wicked man son of a righteous man - one may call him "wicked son of wicked"; a righteous man son of a wicked man - one may call him "righteous son of righteous."

Now, if you see a person who speaks a word or does a deed that can be judged toward good or toward merit, if he is God-fearing you are obligated to judge him favorably, even if the matter leans more toward guilt. And if he is among the intermediate ones, who are careful of sin but sometimes stumble in it, you should tip the doubt to decide in his favor, as they said (Shabbat 127b), "whoever judges his fellow favorably, the Holy One, blessed be He, judges him favorably" - and it is a positive commandment from the Torah (Leviticus 19:15), "in righteousness shall you judge your fellow." And if the matter leans toward guilt, and it is like a doubt, you should decide it toward guilt. And if that man's deeds are mostly evil, or you have tested that there is no fear of God in his heart, decide his deeds and words toward guilt.

And included in this group, that of speaking true slander, is one who mentions to himself alone the evil deeds of his ancestors - behold, he transgresses what is written in the Torah (Leviticus 25:17), "and you shall not wrong one another" - Scripture speaks of wronging with words. If he tells the deeds of his ancestors before others, concerning this our Rabbis said (Bava Metzia 58b), that one who shames his fellow publicly is like one who sheds blood, and descends to Gehinnom and does not ascend. Therefore a person must be careful to distance himself from speaking of people's blemishes and their disgrace, for a person's speech testifies about him and about the hidden matters within him - for the worthy person speaks of people's praises and does not wish to speak of their disgrace, but the unfit person's whole desire is to speak of people's blemishes, for because he himself is unfit he wishes to disqualify others - as we read in Kiddushin (70a): it was taught, whoever disqualifies [others], disqualifies with his own blemish, and does not speak in the world's praise - and Shmuel said, he disqualifies with his own blemish. And if the blemish is well known about him and his family, he must be even more careful to guard his tongue from mentioning it in any manner, even by hint - as they said, of blessed memory, in the chapter "HaZahav" (Bava Metzia 59b), concerning "for you were strangers in the land of Egypt" (Exodus 22:20).

And included in slander is one who speaks it in a manner of jest and levity, meaning that he does not speak out of hatred - and this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 26:18), "like a madman who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, was I not joking?" And likewise one who speaks by way of hints, that he tells it in innocence as though he did not know this matter is slander, but when protested against, says, I did not know this was so-and-so's doing. Also, be careful not to speak slander about charity collectors who are honest, and one who speaks slander about them, saying they steal and show favoritism to whomever they wish - for this slander there is no comparable punishment, for he shames the servants of the LORD and their children and relatives, and prevents good people from performing commandments, and perhaps charity collectors will come who do not do the matter properly [out of discouragement].

The second part: going about as a talebearer - and we are warned about this in the Torah (Leviticus 19:16), "you shall not go about as a talebearer among your people" - and it is included in the group of slanderers, as they said, of blessed memory (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:2), concerning Doeg the Edomite, that he was a master of slander and a talebearer who carried tales - for a talebearer is called one who carries words from this one to that one, "so-and-so said such-and-such about you, he did such-and-such," like this peddler who goes about the towns.

And included in talebearing is being careful about what they said, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 29a): it was taught, from where do we know that a judge should not say, I would acquit but my colleagues obligate, what can I do since they are the majority? Therefore it is said, "you shall not go about as a talebearer among your people."

And the talebearer magnifies hatred, and is found to destroy the pillar of the world, which is peace (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 17). And they said, of blessed memory (Niddah 61a), concerning the matter of talebearing, that although it is forbidden to accept it and hate one's fellow because of it, one should not disdain the matter entirely, but should guard his soul and be wary of the words - and the proof is from Gedaliah ben Achikam, who, because he did not heed accepting slander at all, was killed, as they explained, of blessed memory (ibid.). And they said, of blessed memory (Devarim Rabbah 5:9), that the generation of Saul had among them stirrers of strife, like Doeg and the Ziphites, and although they were righteous, they would go down to war and fall; the generation of Ahab, who had no informers among them, would go down to war and be victorious - for Obadiah hid a hundred prophets and no one revealed it, even though Ahab and his generation were idol-worshippers.

And one who stirs up strife between brothers and friends, and brings hatred between them, is more severe than all the parts of slander, along the lines of what is said (Proverbs 6:19), "and one who sows discord among brothers" - and our Rabbis said (Vayikra Rabbah 16:1) that the seventh [of the seven abominations listed] is more severe than all of them.

Also included in talebearing is not to reveal his fellow's secret, and it is forbidden - for they said in Yoma, first chapter (4b), from where do we know that if one tells his fellow a matter, it is under "you shall not reveal it," that it is forbidden to reveal it? As it is said (Leviticus 1:1), "and the LORD spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying" [implying "do not repeat"]. And whoever reveals a secret departs from the way of modesty - and it appears to me that concerning this it is said, "a talebearer reveals secrets" - meaning, one who reveals secrets is called a talebearer, and he has a punishment just like an actual talebearer, being of the four groups [i.e., extended to a fifth].

The third part: the dust of slander - for they said, of blessed memory, in Bava Batra (165a), that all stumble in the dust of slander - and this has four parts. The first, one who speaks excessively of his fellow's good qualities, for from his good qualities [being mentioned] comes his misfortune - so they said in the chapter "Yesh BeArachin" (16a). And Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, explained (Gate 3, letter 226), that this means he speaks of his fellow's good qualities in the presence of his enemy, and there is no one present at that gathering to protest to the enemy and blunt his teeth - but if he praises a worthy person known for piety, even if an enemy is present, he may praise him, for everyone knows the enemy is lying in his words. And it appears to me that even though one speaks of his fellow's good qualities, he should not speak of them excessively, such as things people will not believe, but only speak of matters and virtues that are believable.

And included in the dust of slander is one who says, where are there coals if not in so-and-so's house, which always roasts meat (Arachin 15b). Further included in this is one who lodges in his fellow's house and is treated well by him, and the next day goes out to the marketplace and says, blessed be so-and-so, who slaughtered such-and-such and prepared such-and-such, and the like - concerning this it is said (Proverbs 27:14), "he who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice," and so on, "it shall be counted a curse to him" - for once the matter is heard, worthless people gather to the host and he loses his money on worthless guests (Arachin 16a). It appears to me that also included in this is: if a person lends his poor fellow a dinar, the poor man should not praise him, for perhaps the host's mind does not agree with everyone, and he might come to a loss, since perhaps they will not repay him properly - and one must be careful.

Included in the dust of slander is what they said in the Talmud there (Arachin 15b), in these words: Rava said, any matter said in the presence of the subject involves no slander. Abaye said to him, all the more so is it brazenness and slander! He said to him, I hold like Rabbi Yosi, who said, in all my days I have never said something and then retracted it - meaning, I never said anything about a person not in his presence that I did not [also] say to his face, in his presence. But if he speaks of one who sinned, and did not first inform the sinner privately and rebuke him, it is accounted to him as slander, for he appears to flatter him [to his face] while revealing his blemish to others not in his presence, and further, they will say of him that he does not speak truth. But if he rebuked him and he did not heed him, then he may inform people of his sin, and they will not suspect him of wishing to cast aspersions on his fellow. And likewise, if the speaker is well known among the many not to show favoritism, and everything he says not in someone's presence he says in their presence, and it is established that he speaks only truth, then it is permitted for him to say those things.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:56-: Further it says there, Rabbah bar Rav Huna said, any matter said in the presence of three involves no slander - why? Because your friend has a friend, and your friend's friend has a friend [so it will spread regardless]. However, if the matter said in the presence of three, or even in the presence of many, was said in confidence, it is forbidden to reveal it - and so they said in Sanhedrin (31a): that student who revealed a matter said in the study hall after twenty-two years, and Rabbi Meir expelled him from the study hall and said, this one reveals secrets - to this point. Also included in the dust of slander, Rambam wrote (Hilchot De'ot, chapter 7, halachah 3), that one should not say, be silent about so-and-so, I do not wish to say what I know about him.

The fourth part is the complainer, and concerning him King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 18:8), "the words of a complainer are like wounds" - and a complainer is a man whose way is to complain and grumble about his fellow, and voice complaints from his heart, saying, so-and-so said such-and-such to me, and his intent was only to insult me, and he intended me harm, even though he intended his good - and he multiplies complaints, and presents himself as oppressed, as though people rob him and insult him and curse him for nothing - and concerning this it is written (Proverbs 16:28), "and a complainer separates close friends" - meaning, he separates from himself a friend and companion. And whoever has this evil quality, just as he complains about people, so he hurls words toward Heaven, and thinks concerning the kindness of the Name that His intent is to take vengeance on His creatures and bring calamity to the world - and even if he sees a bestowal of good, he says it will turn out badly in the end - as it is said (Deuteronomy 1:27), "and you complained in your tents and said, because the LORD hates us," and so on - and our Sages, of blessed memory, said, do not multiply complaints, lest you come to sin. And the complainer, in his evil nature, is ungrateful, for he thinks the good things done for him are evil, and repays evil for good. And this evil quality comes from an evil heart, for from his evil heart he sees a person's good as evil, and brings his evil thought into action, speaking evil and complaining.

The fifth part concerns vulgarity of the mouth, and Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab, peace be upon him, wrote in Sefer Menorat HaMaor (letter 56), in these words: we find that many people are forced with whips, fire, and water, and every kind of coercion, to confess matters for which they are guilty, and they endure all the coercion and do not confess anything with their mouths that would obligate them, through their confession, to execution - and even though they see that it is only a temporary death, for they know for certain that today or tomorrow they will die anyway, nevertheless, in order to gain a temporary life, they endure their distress and accept all the sufferings in the world. All the more so, one who is not forced to say vulgar words, and has no pleasure in this speech, but knows that in saying it, "his iniquity is greater than can be borne," and he shall be judged with everlasting death for it - he should have shut and stopped his mouth from saying it, for whoever speaks vulgarly, his sentence is turned against him for evil - as we read in the first chapter of Ketubot (8b): "therefore the LORD shall not rejoice over their young men," and so on (Isaiah 9:16) - and what is "and His hand is still stretched out"? Rav Chanan bar Abba said, everyone knows why a bride enters the wedding canopy [i.e., for marital relations] - but whoever speaks vulgarly and brings forth a vulgar word from his mouth, even if a decree of seventy good years was sealed for him, it is turned against him for evil.

And we also read in the chapter "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 33a): because of the sin of vulgarity of the mouth, many troubles and evils and harsh decrees are renewed in the world, and the young men of the enemies of Israel [euphemism] die, and orphans and widows cry out and are not answered, as it is said, "therefore the LORD shall not rejoice over their young men," and so on. What is "and His hand is still stretched out"? Rav Chanan said, and so on. And Rav Chisda said, whoever speaks vulgarly, they deepen his Gehinnom, as it is said (Proverbs 22:14), "a deep pit is the mouth of strange women [or: strangers]." Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] says, even one who hears and stays silent, as it is said, "he with whom the LORD is angry shall fall there."

Therefore a person must purify his mouth from speaking vulgarity, for the holy mouth was created only to speak holiness - and one who speaks vulgarly abandons the way of shame and modesty, which are the choice qualities by which Israel are distinguished from the other nations, and shows about himself that he has no share in the holy nation - to this point. And I have shortened some of it so as not to be lengthy. And so Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 3, letter 229).

And concerning the punishment of one who soils his mouth, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pekudei, page 249b) in the palaces of holiness, third palace, in these words: these are four who stand and lend and excommunicate all those who bring forth from their mouths an unnecessary word and soil their mouths - and these excommunicate him, and he remains for forty days during which his prayer is not heard and does not enter the curtain, and he remains rebuked outside - to this point. Behold, he is rebuked and excommunicated, and for forty days his prayer does not ascend above. And it says further there, whoever is excommunicated above, his Maker's protection withdraws from him, and his soul does not ascend above - and we shall copy the rest of his wording below.

Further, in the palaces of impurity (ibid., page 263b), in one palace, in these words: and from this evil spirit hang several other bands, appointed to seize an evil word or a filthy word that a person utters from his mouth, and afterward utters holy words - woe to them, woe to their lives - these are the people who cause those other bands to rule and to blemish a holy place - woe to them in this world, woe to them in the World to Come, for these impure spirits take this impure word, and when a person afterward utters a holy word, these impure spirits get there first and take that impure word and defile that holy word, and the person gains nothing from it, and, as it were, the holy power is weakened - to this point.

And further, they said, of blessed memory (Derech Eretz Rabbah, chapter 3): Rabbi Elazar said, a handsome, praiseworthy person who brings forth a disgraceful word from his mouth - to what is he comparable? To a beautiful hall with a tanner's drainpipe fixed in it - every passerby says, how beautiful this hall is, except that a tanner's drainpipe is in it - to this point.

The sixth part: that he not bring forth a disgraceful word from his mouth - and although they said, a person should always teach his students in a concise manner, it is better to be a bit lengthy so as not to bring forth a disgraceful word from one's mouth - as we read in the first chapter of Pesachim (3a): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, a person should never bring forth a disgraceful word from his mouth, for Scripture went out of its way for eight letters rather than bring forth a disgraceful word from its mouth, as it is said (Genesis 7:8), "and of the animals that are not clean" [rather than saying "impure"]. Rav Ashi said, nine [letters], as it is said (Deuteronomy 23:11), "if there is among you a man who is not clean, because of a nocturnal emission." Rav said, sixteen [letters], as it is said (1 Samuel 20:26), "for he said, something has happened to him, he is not clean, surely he is not clean." And they elaborated further there. And it further says there: there were three priests, one said, my portion came to me doubled (explained as referring to the showbread), one said, my portion came to me the size of an olive, and one said, the size of a lizard's tail - they investigated him and found a taint of disqualification in him - it follows that a person's speech testifies about him and about his root.

And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Submission, chapter 6) wrote, in these words: and it is said of one of the pious ones who passed by a very foul-smelling dog carcass, and his students said to him, how foul-smelling is this carcass! He said to them, how white are its teeth! And they regretted having spoken of its disgrace. And since it is disgraceful to speak of a dead dog, all the more so of a living person - and since it is good to praise a dog's carcass for the whiteness of its teeth, all the more so is it an obligation, by this reasoning, to praise a wise person. And his intent was to rebuke them for not training their tongue to speak evil, lest it become their nature - and so, when they train their tongue to speak good, it shall become their fixed nature, as it is written (Psalms 15:3), "he has no slander on his tongue" - to this point.

The seventh part: not to give his fellow a bad nickname - for they said, of blessed memory, in Bava Metzia (58b): all descend to Gehinnom and ascend, except these, who descend and do not ascend, and these are: one who gives his fellow a bad nickname, one who shames his fellow publicly, and one who has relations with a married woman. Is giving a nickname the same as shaming? [The Talmud answers:] it is necessary [to state both], for even though [the fellow] is accustomed to being called by that name [it is still forbidden] - to this point. Behold, they equated one who gives a bad nickname with one who has relations with a married woman, which is among the severe transgressions for which one must be killed rather than transgress.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 122a), in these words: we have learned, Israel are called "holy," and because they are holy, it is forbidden for people to call their fellow by a disgraceful name, and not to give a nickname to one's fellow, and its punishment is great, all the more so with other words. Rabbi Yosi said, whoever calls his fellow by a name that is not in him, and shames him with it, is caught by what is not in him - for Rabbi Chiya said in the name of Rabbi Chizkiyah, whoever calls his fellow "wicked" brings him down to Gehinnom, and brings down his own worlds [i.e., harms himself], except when the Torah's own strong ones are involved, for a person is permitted to call them wicked - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 13:6-1: And it is explained in the Midrash (Yalkut Tehillim, remez 971), in the psalm "when the Ziphites came" (Psalm 54), that concerning one who speaks slander it is said (Deuteronomy 27:24), "cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret." And so in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 52), in these words: whoever slanders a person in secret has no share in the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 101:5), "whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy" - and one verse says, "cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret." Know that this is so - come and see from the serpent, who slandered Adam to his Maker, and the Holy One, blessed be He, cursed it, that its food would be dust, as it is said (Genesis 3:14), "and dust you shall eat all the days of your life." Rabban Gamliel says, Israel spoke slander against the Holy One, blessed be He, saying, does the LORD have the power to sustain us in the wilderness? As it is said (Psalms 78:19), "and they spoke against God, and said, can God spread a table in the wilderness? Behold, He struck the rock and waters gushed out, and streams overflowed" - and the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that they had slandered His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire, and He sent fire and consumed them all around, as it is said (Numbers 11:1), "and the fire of the LORD burned among them and consumed the edge of the camp." Israel went to Moses and said to him, Moses our teacher, would you have us [given over] like sheep to the slaughter and not to a consuming fire? Moses saw the distress of Israel and prayed - to this point.

And from this teaching you shall see explicitly that the sin of slander blemishes the Shechinah, called His glory, and His glory is a consuming fire - and this is "righteousness, which has no partiality at all" (Zohar, Parashat Balak, page 199a), and it is the angel of whom it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "and do not say before the angel that it was an error" - for even unwitting, it punishes, because it is complete judgment. And this is likewise "this shall be the law of the leper" (Leviticus 14:2), which is explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Metzora) as a sword that avenges vengeance against people who have destroyed with their tongue - and she is called "Zot" [this], on the verse (Job 19:29), "be afraid of the sword for yourselves" - they said, of blessed memory: come and see, through the slander the serpent spoke to the woman, it caused death to be decreed upon the woman, upon Adam, and upon the whole world - concerning slander it is written (Psalms 57:5), "and their tongue a sharp sword" - therefore, "be afraid of the sword for yourselves" - because of slander - "for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword" - what is "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword"? This is the sword belonging to the LORD, for we have learned, the Holy One, blessed be He, has a sword with which He judges the wicked - this is what is written (Isaiah 34:6), "the sword of the LORD is filled with blood," (Deuteronomy 32:42), "and My sword shall devour flesh" - and therefore, "be afraid of the sword for yourselves, for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword" - "that you may know that there is judgment [shaddun]" - so that you know that so he is judged, whoever has a sword in his tongue, a sword is prepared for him that destroys everything - this is what is written, "this shall be the law of the leper" - to this point. And above this it says "shaddun" - written "shadin" - the intent being that he is judged through the supernal sword, which is the attribute of "Zot."

And through what is explained, that one who speaks slander blemishes the Shechinah, a verse from Psalms is understood, which says (Psalms 120:5), "woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech," and so on - and above this it speaks of the matter of slander, "what shall be given to you, and what more shall be done to you, you deceitful tongue" (ibid. 120:3), as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained this matter concerning the slanderer (Midrash Tehillim, ad loc.). And so the following verse proves it, "sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom" - and it explains that the arrows of the mighty are his slanderous words, which are sharp - as King David, peace be upon him, said of Doeg (Psalms 52:3), "why do you boast of evil, O mighty one," and he said (ibid. 64:4), "who sharpen their tongue like a sword, aim their bitter word like an arrow." "With coals of broom" - Rashi explains, in these words: all coals are extinguished on the outside and extinguished on the inside, but these [coals of broom] are extinguished on the outside and not on the inside - to this point. And its explanation is that slander is like the coals of broom, which are not extinguished on the inside - for slander goes and burns little by little, and outwardly it appears extinguished, for he deceives his fellow and speaks peace with him while within he sets his ambush - and this is "deceitful tongue," which the verse mentioned above. And the Shechinah complains about this and says, "woe is me, that I sojourn in Meshech" - meaning, that through his sin he causes the exile to be prolonged, and the Shechinah to dwell with the tents of Kedar, which are the husks.

And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 75b), whose wording we copied, with God's help, in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5, that Israel are delayed in exile because of three matters, because they disgrace the Shechinah, and so on - and all of them are found in slander, for the nakedness of speech is more despised than all, and so [the Shechinah's countenance] turns away from them, along the lines the pious one, peace be upon him, explained, whose wording we copied above.

Further, another explanation, in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 16:5), on the verse mentioned (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth," in these words: "do not let your mouth" - this is Miriam - "and Miriam spoke" (Numbers 12:1). "Cause your flesh to sin" - do not give permission to one of your limbs to cause all your limbs to sin. "And do not say before the angel" - this is Moses, as it is written (ibid. 20:16), "and He sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt." "That it was an error" - "for we have acted foolishly and sinned" (ibid. 12:11). "Why should God be angry at your voice" - "and the anger of the LORD was kindled against them, and He departed" (ibid. 12:9). "And destroy the work of your hands" - through her mouth she sinned, and all the other limbs were struck, as it is written (ibid. 12:10), "and the cloud departed from over the tent," and so on - to this point.

Further there, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, five "Torahs" are written in the passage: "this is the law of the plague of leprosy" (Leviticus 13:59), "this is the law for every plague of leprosy" (ibid. 14:55), "this shall be the law of the leper" (ibid. 14:2), "this is the law for one who has the plague of leprosy" (ibid. 14:32), "this is the law of leprosy" (ibid. 14:57) - "the one who brings forth an evil name" - to teach you that whoever speaks slander transgresses the five books of the Torah - therefore Moses warns Israel - to this point.

Further, in Midrash Tanchuma (Metzora 2): "this shall be the law of the leper" - this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 18:21), "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" - everything depends on the tongue: if it merits, life; if it is liable, death. If a person occupies himself with Torah with his tongue, he merits life, for Torah is a tree of life, as it is said (ibid. 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it," and it is the remedy for slander, as it is said (ibid. 15:4), "a healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it is a break in the spirit." And if a person occupies himself with slander, he becomes liable in his soul to death - for slander is more severe than bloodshed, since a murderer kills only one soul, but the slanderer kills three: the one who says it, the one who accepts it, and the one about whom it is said. For Doeg spoke slander about Achimelech son of Achitov, and he was killed, as it is said (1 Samuel 22:16), "and the king said, you shall surely die, Achimelech" - and Saul was killed, as it is said (1 Chronicles 10:13), "so Saul died for his trespass which he committed against the LORD" - and Saul also said (2 Samuel 1:9), "stand over me and kill me, for the agony [shavatz] has seized me" - the accusation of Nob, the city of priests - and "shavatz" refers only to the priestly garments, as it is said (Exodus 28:13), "and you shall make settings [mishb'tzot] of gold." And Doeg was uprooted from the life of this world and from the life of the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 52:7), "God shall also break you down forever; He shall take you away and pluck you from your tent, and root you out of the land of the living, Selah" - from the life of the World to Come. And in the Jerusalem Talmud (Pe'ah, chapter 1, halachah 1) it says, in the days of Saul there were three who are named [as responsible], and Abner son of Ner, who had the ability to protest and did not protest. Which is more severe, one who strikes with a sword or one who strikes with an arrow? You must say, one who strikes with an arrow - for one who strikes with a sword cannot kill his fellow unless he is close to him and touches him, but one who strikes with an arrow is not so, but rather throws the arrow and strikes him wherever he sees him - therefore the slanderer is likened to an arrow, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow," and so on. And so it says (Psalms 57:5), "the sons of men, their teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword."

And in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, found among us in manuscript, they said, of blessed memory: this is what Scripture says (Job 5:21), "you shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue," and so on - because slander is more severe than a sword. One who has a sword in his hand and seeks to kill his fellow, if he wishes to reconsider, he can, for it is still in his control - but one who wishes to kill his fellow with an arrow, once the arrow has left his hand he cannot reconsider, for the arrow has already left his hand - and so one who speaks slander about his fellow cannot reconsider - and so Scripture testifies concerning them (Jeremiah 9:7), "their tongue is a sharpened arrow" - to this point, relevant here.

Further, in Midrash Tanchuma, in the chapter mentioned, in these words: another interpretation, "death and life are in the hand of the tongue" - slander is so severe that a person does not utter it from his mouth until he denies the fundamental principle, as it is said (Psalms 12:5), "who have said, with our tongue we shall prevail, our lips are with us, who is master over us?" As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, cries out concerning slanderers (ibid. 94:16), "who shall rise up for me against the evildoers," and so on - who can stand against them in Gehinnom? And Gehinnom cries out, I too cannot stand them! He says to it, I am from above and you from below, as it is said (ibid. 120:4), "sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel, do you wish to escape Gehinnom? Distance yourselves from slander, and you shall merit this world and the World to Come, as it is said (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life," and so on, and it is written, "guard your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit," and it is written, "turn from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it." Therefore it is said, "this shall be the law of the leper [metzora]" - "the one who brings forth an evil name [motzi shem ra]" - "motzi ra" - that evil plagues are found [motz'im] on his body.

See what is written concerning Miriam (Numbers 12:1), "and Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses" - therefore (ibid. 12:10), "and Aaron turned to Miriam, and behold, she was leprous." What is written there (Deuteronomy 24:9)? "Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam." Is this not an a fortiori argument? If Miriam, who spoke only of her brother, and intended only to restore him to his wife, was punished thus, one who speaks slander about his fellow, all the more so. What is written above this matter (ibid. 24:8)? "Take heed, in the plague of leprosy, to observe diligently."

And even Aaron, who was High Priest, the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, touched him, as it is said (Numbers 12:9), "and the anger of the LORD was kindled against them, and He departed" - "against them," against both Miriam and Aaron - except that Aaron was healed immediately and Miriam after seven days. This is "this shall be the law of the leper" - "the one who brings forth an evil name" - who found evil.

And so you find concerning the ancient serpent - because it spoke slander against its Creator, it was struck with leprosy. And what did it say? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said (Genesis 3:5), "for on the day you eat of it, your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like God, knowing good and evil" - it said to them, every craftsman hates his fellow [craftsman], and when He wished to create His world, He ate from this tree and created His world - you too, if you eat from it, you can create a world like His. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to it, you spoke slander, in the end you shall be struck with leprosy - as it is said (ibid. 3:14), "and the LORD God said to the serpent, because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle" - with what? With leprosy, as it is said (Leviticus 13:52), "for it is a malignant leprosy." Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Levi, the scales that are on the serpent are its leprosy. And not only that, but all those with blemishes are healed in the World to Come, but the serpent is not healed, as it is said, "cursed are you above all cattle" - from here, that all are healed and it is not healed. Concerning people it is written (Isaiah 35:6), "then shall the lame man leap like a deer," and it is written (ibid. 36... actually different verse), "then the eyes of the blind shall be opened," and so on, and likewise concerning animals and cattle (ibid. 65:25), "the wolf and the lamb shall feed together," and so on, "and the lion shall eat straw like the ox" - but the serpent, "dust shall be its food" - it is never healed, for it brought creatures down to dust - who caused this to it? Because it spoke slander - to this point.

And in the Sifrei it says, in Parashat "and Miriam spoke," behold an a fortiori argument: if Miriam, who did not intend to speak of her brother disparagingly but rather in praise - not to diminish being fruitful and multiplying but to increase it - concerning her brother, who was younger than her, and [spoke only] between herself and him, as it is said (Numbers 12:2), "and the LORD heard," and so on - was punished so, one who intends to speak of his fellow disparagingly and not in praise, to diminish being fruitful and multiplying and not to increase it, concerning one greater than himself, and before others, all the more so. And a further a fortiori argument: if Uzziah the king, who did not intend to take greatness for himself for his own honor but for the honor of the Omnipresent, was punished so, one who intends to take greatness for himself for his own honor, all the more so - to this point.
